Defines the DAG's overall schedule
Names the Airflow connection to use

questions.q: What is the TaskFlow API's @task decorator?
options: A special type of Sensor
A deprecated feature no longer supported in Airflow
A way to delete tasks from a DAG
A lighter-weight alternative to PythonOperator that turns a decorated function into a task automatically
questions.explain: @task does the same job as PythonOperator with less setup — no task_id or python_callable to wire up manually.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when would you still need to read or write classic PythonOperator code?
options: In existing pre-TaskFlow DAGs, cases needing dynamic behavior TaskFlow doesn't cover as cleanly, and older documentation
Only in DAGs that don't use Python at all
Never — TaskFlow has completely replaced PythonOperator in all Airflow versions
Only when using BashOperator instead
questions.explain: Classic PythonOperator still shows up constantly in real codebases and documentation, so recognizing it matters even if @task is more ergonomic for new code.
